jobs.title: CEO
jobs.description:
Acre is proud to be partnering with Fair Trade USA
in the search for their next CEO
.

The Opportunity

Fair Trade USA harnesses the power of markets to build fairer, more resilient global supply chains, improving people's lives, protecting the environment, and demonstrating how everyday commerce can become a powerful force for building a better world.

Fair Trade USA is a fully remote social enterprise of approximately 144 employees with an annual operating budget of approximately $22 million. Through its certification and partner network, Fair Trade Certified generates more than $80 million annually in Community Development Funds benefiting farmers, workers, and fishers around the world.

Yet the opportunity is much greater.

Fair Trade Certified has significant untapped potential to expand buyer and consumer demand and turn the millions of people already connected to Fair Trade - through brands, retailers, workplaces, communities, and everyday purchasing decisions, into more engaged participants and advocates. Our next CEO will lead the effort to unlock that potential, building an organization and movement that makes Fair Trade Certified increasingly meaningful and accessible to consumers, more valuable to brands and retailers, and capable of generating substantially greater impact for producers and workers.

The CEO will have meaningful freedom to innovate and build, supported by an engaged Board and an extraordinary network of employees, producers, brands, retailers, consumers, and other stakeholders.

The CEO Mandate

The CEO will lead Fair Trade USA in building an integrated growth engine connecting:

Integrity and measurable impact → consumer trust and engagement → greater value for brands and retailers → increased demand → greater producer and worker impact.
A central opportunity is to strengthen Fair Trade Certified as a consumer movement, not simply a certification, building relationships with consumers who increasingly understand, trust, seek out, purchase, and advocate for Fair Trade Certified products across brands and categories.
Growth must reinforce, never compromise, the integrity and measurable impact that give Fair Trade Certified its credibility and value.
The CEO will ensure the organization understands and continually improves the processes that drive its impact, measures what works, and allocates people and resources toward the greatest opportunities.

The Leader We Seek

First and foremost, we seek a proven organizational builder and people leader with significant P&L and commercial leadership experience.
We seek a leader driven by purpose and the pursuit of excellence who builds the organization capable of producing exceptional results rather than becoming the source of every important answer.
The successful candidate will be a lifelong learner: curious, self-aware, and able to develop new capabilities, attract strong talent and expertise, and adapt as circumstances change.
Because Fair Trade USA is fully remote, the CEO must also be able to build genuine relationships, trust, engagement, and organizational connection across a distributed workforce, and personally thrive in that environment.

Key Competencies

Strategic judgment and business acumen. Develops and executes strategy with a track record of driving growth. Identifies critical levers, makes difficult trade-offs, allocates resources wisely, and translates strategy into measurable results. Trustworthy and values-driven, holding self and team to a high bar.
Organizational building and people development. Creates shared purpose and priorities, develops leadership throughout the organization, and combines meaningful autonomy with clear accountability. Understands that the organization's long-term strength depends on the people and culture built under their leadership.
Consumer and demand growth. Builds the talent, partnerships, and strategies required to increase buyer and consumer engagement and make Fair Trade Certified more valuable to brands, retailers, and consumers. Brings a track record in consumer brand building or demand generation and can make the business case for Fair Trade in a buyer's language.
Execution discipline and decisiveness. Translates strategy into execution through clear priorities, capable leaders, accountability, and measurable results. Knows when hands-on involvement will provide direction, remove obstacles, develop people, and strengthen engagement; and when stepping back will build greater ownership and organizational capability. Makes tough calls, clearly articulates the why, and ensures commitments are met.
Communication and partnerships. Builds a strong track record of partnerships with major brands and retailers. Communicates clearly and with credibility, adapting their approach for staff, the board, and external partners.
Innovative change agent. Willing to challenge existing models and approaches where the evidence demands it. Keeps Fair Trade USA ahead of a changing economy, digital landscape, and evolving partner and consumer expectations.

A successful CEO will ultimately be known not simply for what they accomplished, but for what Fair Trade Certified became capable of accomplishing under their leadership.

Required Qualifications

Proven C-suite executive leadership, with a track record of organizational performance and results in high-growth environments.
Strong financial acumen and P&L ownership. Demonstrated success managing large-scale budgets and driving sustained year-on-year revenue growth.
Consumer brand or marketing leadership. Proven experience building or scaling a consumer brand or certified product and an understanding of what it takes to earn and hold shelf space.
Demonstrated ability to drive accountability and develop an effective leadership team.
US-based or able to operate with primary presence in the US market, with willingness to travel extensively.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience or knowledge in several of the following areas would strengthen a candidate's fit:

Fair Trade, responsible sourcing, or certification.
Sustainability and assurance.
Consumer products, retail, or related industries, with relevant networks.
Social enterprise or mission-driven organization leadership.
Sales experience and partner development across a diverse stakeholder base.
Board and governance relationships, with strong influencing skills across senior audiences.
Credibility and passion for Fair Trade USA's mission. Culturally competent, with experience working in or with Global South communities.
Experience with distributed or remote organizations.

We can build specialized expertise around an exceptional organizational leader. It is much harder to build exceptional organizational leadership around a functional specialist.
If you would like to be considered for this position, please apply!

Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Connected Warfare division builds systems to support global command and control missions. We create joint, time sensitive, multi domain, ubiquitous, connected mesh ecosystems. Our ecosystem enables connected warfare with disproportional impact by connecting every robot, human, and sensor in every domain, bringing together hundreds of thousands of end points across the globe. We are the substrate that provides the source of truth for time sensitive decisions, effectively transforming the way that militaries close kills chains and enable mission autonomy.

Our Mission Command business line empowers military leaders with advanced command-and-control capabilities by integrating real-time data and actionable insights. We enable agile decision-making and seamless coordination across units, ensuring effective and adaptive operations on the battlefield.

This strategic role owns senior leader engagement within key USMC programs. You will drive rapid fielding of emerging C4I technologies by influencing key stakeholders to ensure organizational readiness. You will proactively engage with the acquisition community to understand and influence USMC technology transformation initiatives. Strong aptitude for problem solving in unstructured situations at the interface of hardware, software, and networking. Ability to drive challenging and vague technical problems to clarity and resolution

Preferred Qualifications

Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. jobs.title: Director of Grants & Institutional Partnerships
jobs.description:
About ReSurge International 

ReSurge International is a global non-profit organization that is scaling up access to reconstructive surgical care in low-income countries by training and supporting the next generation of reconstructive surgeons across Africa, Asia, and Latin America. ReSurge International pairs 55+ years of experience with an innovative empowerment model that is creating a ripple effect of impact across economies, communities, and human lives. ReSurge is at an exciting inflection point of accelerated growth and impact, and we are eager to build a team of passionate and mission-driven individuals who can join us in achieving our goals. 

Position Summary 

ReSurge International is seeking an experienced, relationship-driven fundraising professional to serve as Director of Grants & Institutional Partnerships. This is a high-ownership role that combines strategic stewardship of ReSurge's corporate and foundation funding portfolio with hands-on grant writing and submissions work. You will manage relationships with foundation, corporate, and other institutional funders from cultivation through stewardship, while personally researching, drafting, and submitting compelling grant proposals, letters of inquiry, and funder reports. 

This is an ideal opportunity for a mid-to-senior level grants professional who wants both strategic ownership of a portfolio and the satisfaction of writing the proposals that bring it to life. You will work closely with Programs, Finance, and Communications colleagues to translate ReSurge's surgical training and capacity-building work into funder-ready narratives and data, and you will represent ReSurge in meetings and site visits with corporate and institutional partners. 

This position reports to the Executive Vice President of Programs & Partnerships and will work closely with the broader Development team, program leads across ReSurge's country portfolio, President & CEO, and members of the Board of Directors who support funder relationships. There may be an opportunity for domestic and international travel to meet funders and visit program sites. 
ReSurge seeks an individual who is a confident relationship manager and a skilled, disciplined writer — someone equally comfortable leading a funder strategy conversation and sitting down to draft a proposal narrative or budget justification. Strong project management skills, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple deadlines across a portfolio of funders are essential. Ideal candidates will have a passion for global health equity and, ideally, experience with international development or global health funders. 

Key Responsibilities 

Corporate & Institutional Portfolio Ownership 

● Serve as the primary relationship owner for a portfolio of corporate, foundation, and other institutional funders, managing the full funder lifecycle from prospecting through stewardship and renewal 
● Develop and execute funder-specific engagement strategies in partnership with the EVP of Programs & Partnerships and CEO, aligning ask amounts, timing, and messaging with organizational priorities 
● Build and maintain trusted relationships with funder program officers and corporate giving contacts, serving as a responsive and credible point of contact for ReSurge 
● Track portfolio health, pipeline, and revenue projections, and provide regular reporting to the EVP and CEO on portfolio status and risk 
● Serve as one of the primary representatives of ReSurge in funder meetings, calls, and site visits, including occasional international travel to program sites 

Grant Writing & Submissions 

● Personally research, draft, and submit letters of inquiry, full proposals, budgets, and budget narratives for corporate and institutional funders 
● Partner with Programs and Finance colleagues to gather accurate program data, outcomes, and financials to support compelling, accurate proposal content 
● Write and coordinate timely, high-quality interim and final reports to funders, ensuring compliance with grant terms and reporting schedules 
● Maintain a shared grants calendar and tracking system covering all submission and reporting deadlines across the portfolio 
● Continuously refine core proposal language, case statements, and budget templates to improve consistency and turnaround time 

Prospecting & Portfolio Growth 

● Research and qualify new corporate and institutional funding prospects aligned with ReSurge's mission and program priorities 
● Draft cultivation materials, one-pagers, and concept notes to support new funder outreach 
● Monitor sector trends among corporate and institutional funders in global health and surgical care to identify new opportunities 

Cross-Organization Collaboration & Systems 

● Partner with the Communications team to source stories, photos, and data that strengthen proposals and funder reports 
● Maintain accurate, up-to-date funder records in ReSurge's CRM/database (NXT), including contact history, proposal status, and reporting deadlines 
● Collaborate with Finance to ensure grant budgets and related reporting are thorough, accurate, and audit-compliant 
● Support the CEO, EVP, and board members with briefing materials in advance of funder meetings 

Required Qualifications 

● Bachelor's degree and 5+ years of relevant experience in institutional fundraising, grants management, or grant writing (nonprofit, global health, or international development setting preferred) 
● Demonstrated track record of writing successful grant proposals and managing funder relationships that resulted in secured, multi-year, or renewed funding 
● Exceptional written communication skills, with the ability to translate complex program information into clear, persuasive, funder-ready narratives 
● Strong relationship management skills with the confidence to represent ReSurge directly with senior funder contacts 
● Highly organized, with the project management rigor to manage a portfolio of concurrent deadlines without dropping details 
● Comfortable working with budgets and financial data, and partnering with Finance on grant budgeting and reporting 
● Experience with a CRM or grants management database; familiarity with tools such as Salesforce, Raiser's Edge, or similar is a plus 
● Strong passion and commitment to global health equity and the mission of ReSurge 
● Cultural competency and intercultural communication skills — a respect and curiosity for other world-views 

Work Location 

This position is based in the San Francisco Bay Area. While candidates in the Bay Area are preferred, we’re open to remote candidates within the Pacific/West Coast time zone overlap. This is a full-time, 40-hour per week position; some flexibility is required to accommodate funder meetings and calls across time zones. Evening or weekend hours may occasionally be required for events or deadlines. 

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion 

It is a core belief at ReSurge that diversity, equity, and inclusion make our programs stronger, and we seek to reflect that diversity on our team as well. We are an equal opportunity employer actively seeking diversity in service to our mission to inspire, train, fund, and scale reconstructive surgical teams in low-income countries to provide life-changing care to patients with the greatest need. 

Compensation 

Commensurate with qualifications and experience, plus excellent health benefits, 401(k) retirement plan with employer matching up to 4% of salary, a flexible work schedule, and generous paid time off. 
Salary Range: $90,000–$120,000 

To Apply 

Please submit a letter of interest and resume by email to jobs@resurge.org with the subject line: Director of Grants & Institutional Partnerships. Please apply by 5:00 PM PT on Friday, September 11, 2026.
Applications received after this time will not be considered.

Evaluate facility utilization practices and recommend improvements that maximize resources and enhance the school experience for students, staff, families, and communities.

Job Description

CEO/General Manager

Gem City Market – Dayton, Ohio

Retained Search Partner: The Carlisle Group

Salary Range: $90,000 – $115,000

The Carlisle Group is pleased to be partnered on a retained search with Gem City Market
in Dayton, Ohio, in the search for their next CEO/General Manager
.

Gem City Market is a community-centered, full-service grocery cooperative created to bring quality, affordable food to a diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood in Dayton. More than simply a grocery store, Gem City Market is committed to being a pillar of the community it serves—helping strengthen the local culture, creating opportunity, and providing a welcoming place where neighbors can shop, connect, and thrive.

The co-op is seeking an entrepreneurial, community-minded grocery leader who can balance mission and margin
—someone who understands that a successful cooperative must deliver both meaningful community impact and strong financial performance. The CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to lead the Market into its next chapter while ensuring that customers receive quality products at affordable prices in a clean, welcoming, and inclusive environment.

Living in Dayton

Dayton offers an appealing combination of affordability, accessibility, community, and opportunity
. Located in southwest Ohio, Dayton provides the amenities of a larger metropolitan area while retaining a strong sense of neighborhood and community.

The city has a rich history of innovation, entrepreneurship, and community involvement and is home to a diverse collection of neighborhoods, restaurants, arts and cultural attractions, parks, and outdoor recreation. Residents enjoy access to an extensive regional park system, the great Miami River, biking and hiking trails, and numerous opportunities to enjoy the outdoors.

Dayton's location is another advantage. Cincinnati and Columbus are both within approximately an hour's drive, while Cleveland and Indianapolis are accessible within a few hours. The region offers a relatively affordable cost of living compared with many larger U.S. metropolitan areas, making Dayton an attractive place to build both a career and a life.

For a leader who wants to make a tangible difference in a community while enjoying a high quality of life, Dayton presents a compelling opportunity.

Position Purpose

The CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading Gem City Market as a successful, financially sustainable cooperative while advancing the goals and purposes established by the Board of Directors.

The CEO/General Manager Will Ensure That The Market

Operates efficiently and ultimately profitably.
Provides quality, affordable groceries that meet the needs of its customers.
Maintains a clean, welcoming, and inclusive shopping environment.
Builds a positive culture for employees and the broader community.
Advances the cooperative's mission and role as a community institution.
Remains responsive to the needs of the diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood it serves.

The CEO/General Manager will bring together the disciplines of grocery operations, financial management, merchandising, people leadership, marketing, and community engagement
to ensure the continued success of Gem City Market.

Overview Of Responsibilities

Operations

Lead an efficient, customer-focused, and ultimately profitable cooperative grocery operation.
Create a positive store atmosphere and build a motivated, accountable staff team.
Maintain current knowledge of grocery retailing, industry trends, and best practices, particularly those applicable to cooperative markets and urban, low- to moderate-income communities.
Develop and maintain productive relationships with market partners, wholesale distributors, local markets, and other industry resources.
Establish and maintain an appropriate product mix that meets shopper needs while supporting financial objectives.
Develop and execute a margin strategy that allows Gem City Market to remain price competitive while maintaining adequate cash flow.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, licenses, permits, health requirements, and employment standards.
Continuously evaluate operational performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, customer service, and profitability.

Financial Management & Strategic Planning

Develop and recommend long- and short-range plans designed to achieve the cooperative's purposes and strategic objectives.
Direct the financial operations of the cooperative and maintain accountability for the organization's financial performance.
Develop operating, capital, and cash budgets for Board approval and manage the business within approved financial parameters.
Provide regular, meaningful financial and operational reporting to the Board of Directors.
Monitor key grocery industry metrics and use financial and operational data to make informed decisions.
Identify new business opportunities and make recommendations to the Board regarding potential growth, partnerships, and innovation.
Participate in regional and national cooperative and grocery industry events to remain connected to emerging trends and best practices.

People & Culture

Determine the appropriate staffing structure and maintain clear, effective job descriptions.
Hire management personnel and oversee the hiring, training, development, and retention of Market staff.
Create a positive, productive, inclusive, and accountable workplace culture.
Manage and evaluate employees while providing timely coaching, feedback, recognition, and accountability.
Establish appropriate compensation structures based upon the budget, local labor market, and competitive conditions.

The Business Council for Sustainable Energy (BCSE) is a coalition of companies and trade associations that deploy clean energy and decarbonization solutions, with a sector focus on energy efficiency, natural gas, renewable energy, energy storage, sustainable transportation, and other technologies. BCSE advocates for policies that support a diverse portfolio of energy options in the United States and expand access to affordable, reliable, and clean and efficient energy solutions.

Established in 1992, BCSE members include investor-owned utilities, public power, independent power producers, project developers, technology providers, equipment manufacturers, environmental and energy market service companies, and trade associations. BCSE is a member-driven organization that develops policy positions and advocacy strategies through active member committees and direct engagement with policymakers and stakeholders. For more information, visit bcse.org.

About the Director of Government Relations Position 

BCSE is seeking a Director of Government Relations to lead the coalition’s education and advocacy on federal and state policy. This position will serve as a senior member of a small, highly collaborative team and will work directly with BCSE leadership, member companies and associations, policymakers, regulators, and allied organizations to advance the coalition’s policy priorities. The position is based in Washington, DC.

Responsibilities include: 

Support BCSE’s federal and state government relations portfolio, including education, advocacy, legislative engagement, regulatory strategy, and stakeholder outreach.
Manage BCSE member policy committees, including developing work plans, setting agendas, preparing materials, facilitating meetings, inviting and coordinating guest speakers and outreach activities.
Work with BCSE leadership and members to identify policy objectives that reflect the coalition’s diverse membership and advance durable market opportunities for sustainable energy solutions.
Develop and implement education and advocacy strategies, including policymaker outreach, briefings, coalition letters, comments, testimony, talking points, policy memos, and stakeholder events.
Monitor, analyze, and communicate federal and state legislative and regulatory developments affecting BCSE members, identifying emerging risks, opportunities, and recommended courses of action.
Represent BCSE in external coalitions, trade association working groups, regulatory stakeholder processes, conferences, briefings, and public forums.
Coordinate BCSE engagement with Congress and federal agencies and executive branch officials on energy, tax, environmental, infrastructure, appropriations, permitting, market, and related policy matters.
Develop and maintain relationships with state policymakers, regional organizations, and other relevant state and regional stakeholders, as necessary.
Represent BCSE in external coalitions, conferences, briefings, and public forums, as needed.
Prepare clear, concise issue summaries, presentations, and advocacy materials that translate legislative, regulatory, and market issues for members and policymakers.
Support compliance with applicable lobbying, ethics, and reporting requirements in coordination with BCSE leadership and advisors.

Qualified candidates should have three to five years of experience in government relations, public policy, regulatory affairs, energy policy, or a closely related field, with meaningful experience at both the federal and state levels.
Experience with federal state legislative and regulatory processes and the ability to assess how state and regional developments interact with federal policy and energy markets.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare persuasive policy materials and communicate complex issues clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Strong judgment, political awareness, discretion, and the ability to identify when issues require rapid escalation or senior-level engagement.
Ability to manage multiple complex policy matters simultaneously, prioritize effectively, meet deadlines, and operate with a high degree of independence in a small-team environment.
Collaborative working style, attention to detail, and willingness to contribute across functions when needed.

This is a full-time, in-person position. Compensation will be commensurate with experience and qualifications. BCSE offers paid annual leave, participation in its 401(k) retirement program, and other benefits.

About ReSurge International 

ReSurge International is a global non-profit organization that is scaling up access to reconstructive surgical care in low-income countries by training and supporting the next generation of reconstructive surgeons across Africa, Asia, and Latin America. ReSurge International pairs 55+ years of experience with an innovative empowerment model that is creating a ripple effect of impact across economies, communities, and human lives. ReSurge is at an exciting inflection point of accelerated growth and impact, and we are eager to build a team of passionate and mission-driven individuals who can join us in achieving our goals. 

Position Summary 

ReSurge International is seeking an experienced, relationship-driven fundraising professional to serve as Director of Grants & Institutional Partnerships. This is a high-ownership role that combines strategic stewardship of ReSurge's corporate and foundation funding portfolio with hands-on grant writing and submissions work. You will manage relationships with foundation, corporate, and other institutional funders from cultivation through stewardship, while personally researching, drafting, and submitting compelling grant proposals, letters of inquiry, and funder reports. 

This is an ideal opportunity for a mid-to-senior level grants professional who wants both strategic ownership of a portfolio and the satisfaction of writing the proposals that bring it to life. You will work closely with Programs, Finance, and Communications colleagues to translate ReSurge's surgical training and capacity-building work into funder-ready narratives and data, and you will represent ReSurge in meetings and site visits with corporate and institutional partners. 

This position reports to the Executive Vice President of Programs & Partnerships and will work closely with the broader Development team, program leads across ReSurge's country portfolio, President & CEO, and members of the Board of Directors who support funder relationships. There may be an opportunity for domestic and international travel to meet funders and visit program sites. 
ReSurge seeks an individual who is a confident relationship manager and a skilled, disciplined writer — someone equally comfortable leading a funder strategy conversation and sitting down to draft a proposal narrative or budget justification. Strong project management skills, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple deadlines across a portfolio of funders are essential. Ideal candidates will have a passion for global health equity and, ideally, experience with international development or global health funders. 

Key Responsibilities 

Corporate & Institutional Portfolio Ownership 

● Serve as the primary relationship owner for a portfolio of corporate, foundation, and other institutional funders, managing the full funder lifecycle from prospecting through stewardship and renewal 
● Develop and execute funder-specific engagement strategies in partnership with the EVP of Programs & Partnerships and CEO, aligning ask amounts, timing, and messaging with organizational priorities 
● Build and maintain trusted relationships with funder program officers and corporate giving contacts, serving as a responsive and credible point of contact for ReSurge 
● Track portfolio health, pipeline, and revenue projections, and provide regular reporting to the EVP and CEO on portfolio status and risk 
● Serve as one of the primary representatives of ReSurge in funder meetings, calls, and site visits, including occasional international travel to program sites 

Grant Writing & Submissions 

● Personally research, draft, and submit letters of inquiry, full proposals, budgets, and budget narratives for corporate and institutional funders 
● Partner with Programs and Finance colleagues to gather accurate program data, outcomes, and financials to support compelling, accurate proposal content 
● Write and coordinate timely, high-quality interim and final reports to funders, ensuring compliance with grant terms and reporting schedules 
● Maintain a shared grants calendar and tracking system covering all submission and reporting deadlines across the portfolio 
● Continuously refine core proposal language, case statements, and budget templates to improve consistency and turnaround time 

Prospecting & Portfolio Growth 

● Research and qualify new corporate and institutional funding prospects aligned with ReSurge's mission and program priorities 
● Draft cultivation materials, one-pagers, and concept notes to support new funder outreach 
● Monitor sector trends among corporate and institutional funders in global health and surgical care to identify new opportunities 

Cross-Organization Collaboration & Systems 

● Partner with the Communications team to source stories, photos, and data that strengthen proposals and funder reports 
● Maintain accurate, up-to-date funder records in ReSurge's CRM/database (NXT), including contact history, proposal status, and reporting deadlines 
● Collaborate with Finance to ensure grant budgets and related reporting are thorough, accurate, and audit-compliant 
● Support the CEO, EVP, and board members with briefing materials in advance of funder meetings 

Required Qualifications 

● Bachelor's degree and 5+ years of relevant experience in institutional fundraising, grants management, or grant writing (nonprofit, global health, or international development setting preferred) 
● Demonstrated track record of writing successful grant proposals and managing funder relationships that resulted in secured, multi-year, or renewed funding 
● Exceptional written communication skills, with the ability to translate complex program information into clear, persuasive, funder-ready narratives 
● Strong relationship management skills with the confidence to represent ReSurge directly with senior funder contacts 
● Highly organized, with the project management rigor to manage a portfolio of concurrent deadlines without dropping details 
● Comfortable working with budgets and financial data, and partnering with Finance on grant budgeting and reporting 
● Experience with a CRM or grants management database; familiarity with tools such as Salesforce, Raiser's Edge, or similar is a plus 
● Strong passion and commitment to global health equity and the mission of ReSurge 
● Cultural competency and intercultural communication skills — a respect and curiosity for other world-views 

Work Location 

This position is based in the San Francisco Bay Area. While candidates in the Bay Area are preferred, we’re open to remote candidates within the Pacific/West Coast time zone overlap. This is a full-time, 40-hour per week position; some flexibility is required to accommodate funder meetings and calls across time zones. Evening or weekend hours may occasionally be required for events or deadlines. 

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion 

It is a core belief at ReSurge that diversity, equity, and inclusion make our programs stronger, and we seek to reflect that diversity on our team as well. We are an equal opportunity employer actively seeking diversity in service to our mission to inspire, train, fund, and scale reconstructive surgical teams in low-income countries to provide life-changing care to patients with the greatest need. 

Compensation 

Commensurate with qualifications and experience, plus excellent health benefits, 401(k) retirement plan with employer matching up to 4% of salary, a flexible work schedule, and generous paid time off. 
Salary Range: $90,000–$120,000 

To Apply 

Please submit a letter of interest and resume by email to jobs@resurge.org with the subject line: Director of Grants & Institutional Partnerships. Please apply by 5:00 PM PT on Friday, September 11, 2026.

in Dayton, Ohio, in the search for their next CEO/General Manager
.

Gem City Market is a community-centered, full-service grocery cooperative created to bring quality, affordable food to a diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood in Dayton. More than simply a grocery store, Gem City Market is committed to being a pillar of the community it serves—helping strengthen the local culture, creating opportunity, and providing a welcoming place where neighbors can shop, connect, and thrive.

The co-op is seeking an entrepreneurial, community-minded grocery leader who can balance mission and margin
—someone who understands that a successful cooperative must deliver both meaningful community impact and strong financial performance. The CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to lead the Market into its next chapter while ensuring that customers receive quality products at affordable prices in a clean, welcoming, and inclusive environment.

Living in Dayton

Dayton offers an appealing combination of affordability, accessibility, community, and opportunity
. Located in southwest Ohio, Dayton provides the amenities of a larger metropolitan area while retaining a strong sense of neighborhood and community.

The city has a rich history of innovation, entrepreneurship, and community involvement and is home to a diverse collection of neighborhoods, restaurants, arts and cultural attractions, parks, and outdoor recreation. Residents enjoy access to an extensive regional park system, the great Miami River, biking and hiking trails, and numerous opportunities to enjoy the outdoors.

Dayton's location is another advantage. Cincinnati and Columbus are both within approximately an hour's drive, while Cleveland and Indianapolis are accessible within a few hours. The region offers a relatively affordable cost of living compared with many larger U.S. metropolitan areas, making Dayton an attractive place to build both a career and a life.

For a leader who wants to make a tangible difference in a community while enjoying a high quality of life, Dayton presents a compelling opportunity.

Position Purpose

The CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading Gem City Market as a successful, financially sustainable cooperative while advancing the goals and purposes established by the Board of Directors.

The CEO/General Manager Will Ensure That The Market

Operates efficiently and ultimately profitably.
Provides quality, affordable groceries that meet the needs of its customers.
Maintains a clean, welcoming, and inclusive shopping environment.
Builds a positive culture for employees and the broader community.
Advances the cooperative's mission and role as a community institution.
Remains responsive to the needs of the diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood it serves.

The CEO/General Manager will bring together the disciplines of grocery operations, financial management, merchandising, people leadership, marketing, and community engagement
to ensure the continued success of Gem City Market.

Overview Of Responsibilities

Operations

Lead an efficient, customer-focused, and ultimately profitable cooperative grocery operation.
Create a positive store atmosphere and build a motivated, accountable staff team.
Maintain current knowledge of grocery retailing, industry trends, and best practices, particularly those applicable to cooperative markets and urban, low- to moderate-income communities.
Develop and maintain productive relationships with market partners, wholesale distributors, local markets, and other industry resources.
Establish and maintain an appropriate product mix that meets shopper needs while supporting financial objectives.
Develop and execute a margin strategy that allows Gem City Market to remain price competitive while maintaining adequate cash flow.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, licenses, permits, health requirements, and employment standards.
Continuously evaluate operational performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, customer service, and profitability.

Financial Management & Strategic Planning

Develop and recommend long- and short-range plans designed to achieve the cooperative's purposes and strategic objectives.
Direct the financial operations of the cooperative and maintain accountability for the organization's financial performance.
Develop operating, capital, and cash budgets for Board approval and manage the business within approved financial parameters.
Provide regular, meaningful financial and operational reporting to the Board of Directors.
Monitor key grocery industry metrics and use financial and operational data to make informed decisions.
Identify new business opportunities and make recommendations to the Board regarding potential growth, partnerships, and innovation.
Participate in regional and national cooperative and grocery industry events to remain connected to emerging trends and best practices.

People & Culture

Determine the appropriate staffing structure and maintain clear, effective job descriptions.
Hire management personnel and oversee the hiring, training, development, and retention of Market staff.
Create a positive, productive, inclusive, and accountable workplace culture.
Manage and evaluate employees while providing timely coaching, feedback, recognition, and accountability.
Establish appropriate compensation structures based upon the budget, local labor market, and competitive conditions.
Organize staffing to promote a fair distribution of work while maintaining excellent customer service.
Develop and maintain an effective employee benefits program.
Build a culture where employees understand the Market's mission and their role in delivering it.

Marketing & Community Engagement

Develop and execute an effective advertising and marketing strategy that maintains strong public awareness of Gem City Market and its products and services.
Ensure marketing activities are executed within established budgetary guidelines.
Communicate effectively with cooperative members, customers, employees, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Prepare or oversee the preparation of the annual report and other communications to the cooperative's members and community.
Ensure that store displays, signage, promotions, and merchandising effectively support sales and customer engagement.
Strengthen Gem City Market's position as a trusted and visible community institution.
Identify opportunities to deepen relationships with local organizations, businesses, producers, and community partners.

Reporting Relationships

The CEO/General Manager reports directly to the Board of Directors
, which includes Market staff and members of the community.

The Board is responsible for establishing the organization's overall direction, goals, and expectations, while the CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading day-to-day operations and executing the strategy established by the Board.

The CEO/General Manager has the authority to hire, direct, structure, develop, and evaluate all other Market staff.

The successful candidate will understand the importance of building a strong, collaborative relationship with the Board based on trust, transparency, accountability, and open communication
.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will bring a combination of grocery retail expertise, financial acumen, leadership ability, entrepreneurial thinking, and a genuine commitment to community.

Grocery Retail Leadership

Minimum of five years of successful experience managing a retail grocery store.
Strong understanding of grocery store operations and the various departments required to achieve sales, margin, labor, and profitability goals.
Demonstrated understanding of key grocery industry metrics and how to use them to drive performance.
Experience managing both retail and administrative functions.
Knowledge of current grocery industry trends and competitive dynamics.
Experience with merchandising and marketing in highly competitive grocery markets.

Financial Management

Demonstrated bottom-line accountability for a grocery or retail operation.
Strong understanding of financial variables and their relationship to overall business performance.
Experience developing and managing operating, capital, and cash budgets.
Ability to analyze financial and operational information and translate it into effective business decisions.
Demonstrated ability to balance affordability and customer needs with margin, cash flow, and profitability requirements.

Leadership & People Management

Proven ability to motivate, lead, and coordinate people to achieve organizational objectives.
Experience hiring, training, evaluating, developing, compensating, and, when necessary, terminating employees.
Ability to establish clear expectations and hold people accountable.
Strong listening skills and the ability to both give and receive constructive feedback.
Self-aware, self-motivated, and comfortable taking ownership of decisions and outcomes.
Ability to handle multiple priorities and demands while maintaining focus on the organization's most important objectives.

Cooperative & Community Leadership

Genuine understanding of and appreciation for the cooperative business model.
Ability to articulate what makes a cooperative different and how cooperative principles influence decision-making.
Experience working effectively with a Board of Directors.
Ability to build trust with Board members, employees, customers, and community stakeholders.
Service-oriented leadership style with a genuine interest in improving the community served by the organization.
Experience working in a food desert, food-insecure, or low-income community is highly valued.

Strategic & Entrepreneurial Thinking

Ability to make difficult decisions and take appropriate risks when necessary.
Strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify root causes and develop practical solutions.
Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to recognize and pursue opportunities for innovation and growth.
Ability to maintain momentum and lead change with a sense of urgency.

Ability to balance immediate operational demands with the long-term health and sustainability of the cooperative.

The Opportunity

This is a unique opportunity for a hands-on grocery leader and community-minded executive
to lead an organization with a purpose that extends well beyond the four walls of a grocery store.

The next CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to strengthen Gem City Market's financial and operational performance while helping fulfill its larger role as a source of affordable food, employment, connection, and opportunity within the Dayton community.

For the right leader, this is more than an opportunity to run a grocery store. It is an opportunity to help build a stronger community through grocery retail.

, for more information regarding this retained search at bcm@tcgrecruit.com
.

The Business Council for Sustainable Energy (BCSE) is a coalition of companies and trade associations that deploy clean energy and decarbonization solutions, with a sector focus on energy efficiency, natural gas, renewable energy, energy storage, sustainable transportation, and other technologies. BCSE advocates for policies that support a diverse portfolio of energy options in the United States and expand access to affordable, reliable, and clean and efficient energy solutions.

Established in 1992, BCSE members include investor-owned utilities, public power, independent power producers, project developers, technology providers, equipment manufacturers, environmental and energy market service companies, and trade associations. BCSE is a member-driven organization that develops policy positions and advocacy strategies through active member committees and direct engagement with policymakers and stakeholders. For more information, visit bcse.org.

About the Director of Government Relations Position 

BCSE is seeking a Director of Government Relations to lead the coalition’s education and advocacy on federal and state policy. This position will serve as a senior member of a small, highly collaborative team and will work directly with BCSE leadership, member companies and associations, policymakers, regulators, and allied organizations to advance the coalition’s policy priorities. The position is based in Washington, DC.

Responsibilities include: 

Support BCSE’s federal and state government relations portfolio, including education, advocacy, legislative engagement, regulatory strategy, and stakeholder outreach.
Manage BCSE member policy committees, including developing work plans, setting agendas, preparing materials, facilitating meetings, inviting and coordinating guest speakers and outreach activities.
Work with BCSE leadership and members to identify policy objectives that reflect the coalition’s diverse membership and advance durable market opportunities for sustainable energy solutions.
Develop and implement education and advocacy strategies, including policymaker outreach, briefings, coalition letters, comments, testimony, talking points, policy memos, and stakeholder events.
Monitor, analyze, and communicate federal and state legislative and regulatory developments affecting BCSE members, identifying emerging risks, opportunities, and recommended courses of action.
Represent BCSE in external coalitions, trade association working groups, regulatory stakeholder processes, conferences, briefings, and public forums.
Coordinate BCSE engagement with Congress and federal agencies and executive branch officials on energy, tax, environmental, infrastructure, appropriations, permitting, market, and related policy matters.
Develop and maintain relationships with state policymakers, regional organizations, and other relevant state and regional stakeholders, as necessary.
Represent BCSE in external coalitions, conferences, briefings, and public forums, as needed.
Prepare clear, concise issue summaries, presentations, and advocacy materials that translate legislative, regulatory, and market issues for members and policymakers.
Support compliance with applicable lobbying, ethics, and reporting requirements in coordination with BCSE leadership and advisors.

Qualifications 

Qualified candidates should have three to five years of experience in government relations, public policy, regulatory affairs, energy policy, or a closely related field, with meaningful experience at both the federal and state levels.
Experience with federal state legislative and regulatory processes and the ability to assess how state and regional developments interact with federal policy and energy markets.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare persuasive policy materials and communicate complex issues clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Strong judgment, political awareness, discretion, and the ability to identify when issues require rapid escalation or senior-level engagement.
Ability to manage multiple complex policy matters simultaneously, prioritize effectively, meet deadlines, and operate with a high degree of independence in a small-team environment.
Collaborative working style, attention to detail, and willingness to contribute across functions when needed.

Utilizing innovative clinical research, cutting-edge technologies, and advanced treatments, we are committed to providing world-class cancer care. Come join us today!

Summary

The Managing Director, Strategic Initiatives, Transformation & PMO serves as an enterprise execution partner to the Chief Executive Officer and Executive Leadership Team (ELT), responsible for translating approved strategic priorities into coordinated enterprise execution. The role leads the Enterprise Transformation Office (ETO) and Program Management Office (PMO), overseeing portfolio governance, prioritization, organizational transformation, executive governance processes, enterprise change management standards, and strategic initiative execution. The position ensures enterprise initiatives are appropriately governed, resourced, sequenced, monitored, and aligned to organizational priorities while supporting successful implementation and benefit realization. The role partners with business leaders, functional teams, Business Development, diligence teams, a separate integration team, and operational stakeholders to coordinate execution, manage dependencies, monitor risks, support organizational readiness, and facilitate successful implementation from planning through stabilization. The position operates with a high degree of independence, discretion, and influence and achieves results primarily through collaboration, facilitation, governance, accountability, and executive stakeholder management rather than direct organizational authority. Business leaders retain ownership of operational decisions, business outcomes, and benefit realization; this role owns governance, visibility, coordination, accountability processes, escalation, and execution support.

Primary Tasks And Responsibilities

ENTERPRISE TRANSFORMATION & PORTFOLIO GOVERNANCE

Lead the Enterprise Transformation Office (ETO) and Program Management Office (PMO), establishing governance processes, methodologies, tools, reporting standards, and execution disciplines across the organization.
Own governance of the enterprise portfolio of approved strategic initiatives, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities, available capacity, resource constraints, dependencies, and timelines.
Facilitate enterprise prioritization processes and support annual and ongoing strategic planning activities by coordinating inputs, documenting decisions, translating priorities into implementation plans, and monitoring execution.
Develop enterprise portfolio dashboards, executive reports, scorecards, and performance metrics to provide visibility into initiative status, risks, dependencies, milestones, and outcomes.
Establish and enforce governance standards requiring defined business ownership, milestones, resource plans, risk assessments, dependency management, success metrics, and recovery actions for major initiatives.
Monitor initiative progress and benefit-realization plans while ensuring accountable business leaders retain ownership of operational decisions, business outcomes, and realized benefits.

STRATEGIC INITIATIVE EXECUTION

Support execution of approved strategic priorities through stakeholder alignment, initiative coordination, dependency management, readiness planning, issue resolution, and progress monitoring.
Directly manage select CEO-sponsored strategic initiatives while coordinating execution support for broader enterprise initiatives led by accountable business owners.
Facilitate cross-functional collaboration across operational, clinical, administrative, and technology teams to advance approved organizational priorities.
Identify execution barriers, resource constraints, competing priorities, and implementation risks, and work with business leaders to develop mitigation and recovery plans.
Challenge insufficient plans and elevate unresolved risks, resource constraints, or missed commitments to the CEO and ELT while preserving business-leader accountability for outcomes.

EXECUTIVE GOVERNANCE & LEADERSHIP CADENCE

Coordinate executive governance processes, leadership operating cadences, decision tracking, accountability reviews, and enterprise follow-through mechanisms in partnership with the CEO, ELT, and business leaders.
Support agenda development, content preparation, meeting coordination, action management, and follow-through for ELT, Leadership Team, Extended Leadership Team, and other executive governance forums.
Ensure executive decisions are clearly documented, communicated, assigned, tracked, and monitored through completion.
Provide executive leadership with transparent updates regarding initiative status, organizational risks, execution challenges, and enterprise dependencies.

BOARD GOVERNANCE & EXECUTIVE REPORTING

Coordinate board governance activities, executive reporting processes, and board material preparation in partnership with the CEO, executive leadership, legal counsel, and functional leaders.
Contribute to the development of board presentations, executive summaries, implementation updates, and strategic initiative reporting.
Maintain rigorous standards for quality, consistency, version control, confidentiality, and timeliness of executive and board materials.

TRANSFORMATION, INTEGRATION & ORGANIZATIONAL READINESS

Coordinate governance, milestone oversight, dependency management, and readiness activities supporting strategic affiliations, partnerships, technology implementations, organizational transformations, and other enterprise initiatives.
Serve as the program-management bridge among Business Development, functional diligence teams, the separate integration team, and operational leaders to support the transition from Business Development through diligence and execution toward go-live.
Support the integration team through implementation, go-live readiness, stabilization, and benefit-realization governance without assuming transaction leadership, functional diligence ownership, or day-to-day integration ownership.
Monitor organizational readiness and implementation preparedness across impacted departments and stakeholders.
Support post-implementation stabilization and ensure lessons learned are captured and applied to future initiatives.

CHANGE MANAGEMENT & ADOPTION

Establish and maintain enterprise change-management standards, methodologies, frameworks, tools, and governance processes.
Assess organizational readiness and adoption risks associated with major enterprise initiatives.
Ensure major initiatives include effective stakeholder engagement, communication, training, readiness, and adoption plans.
Partner with business leaders, Human Resources, Communications, Learning & Development, and project teams to support local execution and adoption of organizational change.
Track and report change-management effectiveness and readiness indicators across major transformation efforts.

COMMUNICATIONS & STAKEHOLDER ENGAGEMENT

Partner with executive and business leaders to coordinate and contribute to enterprise communications, leadership messaging, organizational announcements, stakeholder engagement, and change-management communications related to strategic initiatives.
Support development of town hall materials, executive talking points, leadership presentations, implementation updates, and transformation-related communications.
Facilitate alignment across stakeholders with competing priorities, perspectives, and interests.

Leadership & Additional Responsibilities

Lead primarily through influence and matrix management, with a limited number of direct reports as organizational needs require.
Coach leaders and project sponsors in governance, accountability, execution discipline, change leadership, and transformation management.
Maintain confidentiality regarding strategic initiatives, leadership matters, organizational changes, legal matters, board activities, and other sensitive information.
Negotiate priorities, resolve issues, and explore solutions with physician and clinical leaders.
Perform other duties and projects as assigned.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About The Team

The Connected Warfare division builds systems to support global command and control missions. We create joint, time sensitive, multi domain, ubiquitous, connected mesh ecosystems. Our ecosystem enables connected warfare with disproportional impact by connecting every robot, human, and sensor in every domain, bringing together hundreds of thousands of end points across the globe. We are the substrate that provides the source of truth for time sensitive decisions, effectively transforming the way that militaries close kills chains and enable mission autonomy.

Our Mission Command business line empowers military leaders with advanced command-and-control capabilities by integrating real-time data and actionable insights. We enable agile decision-making and seamless coordination across units, ensuring effective and adaptive operations on the battlefield.

This strategic role owns senior leader engagement within key USMC programs. You will drive rapid fielding of emerging C4I technologies by influencing key stakeholders to ensure organizational readiness. You will proactively engage with the acquisition community to understand and influence USMC technology transformation initiatives. Success requires a high-integrity individual capable of objectively translating complex technical principles into compelling operational outcomes.
